case_studies.title: TSCG: Deterministic Tool-Schema Compilation for Agentic LLM Deployments
case_studies.abstract: Production agent frameworks (OpenAI Function Calling, Anthropic Tool Use, MCP) transmit tool schemas as JSON, a format designed for machine parsing, not for interpretation by language models. For small models (4B-14B), this protocol mismatch accounts for the majority of tool-use failure at production catalog sizes. We present TSCG, a deterministic tool-schema compiler that resolves this mismatch at the API boundary, converting JSON schemas into token-efficient structured text without model access, fine-tuning, or runtime search. TSCG combines eight composable operators with a formal compressio
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of tool-schema compilation for large language models by building a deterministic tool-schema compiler called TSCG, which converts JSON schemas into structured text, resulting in improved tool-use success rates. TSCG achieves this without requiring model access, fine-tuning, or runtime search. This research is relevant to IT engineers managing cloud infrastructure that utilizes large language models.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage large language model deployments, here is what to do: assess your current tool-schema compilation process, consider implementing TSCG to improve tool-use success rates, and evaluate the potential benefits of using TSCG in your production environment.
case_studies.score_reasoning: High IT_RELEVANCE and VALUE_90_DAYS for its impact on deployable, agentic LLMs; NOVELTY for deterministic compilation; low VALUE_90_DAYS as it is purely academic (no real-world use case or application in 90 days)

case_studies.title: When and Why SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Theoretical Study Based on $\ell_1$-norm Lower Bounds
case_studies.abstract: Sign-based optimization algorithms, such as SignSGD and Muon, have garnered significant attention for their remarkable performance in training large foundation models. Despite this empirical success, we still lack a theoretical understanding of when and why these sign-based methods outperform vanilla SGD. case_studies.title: Online Bayesian Calibration under Gradual and Abrupt System Changes
case_studies.abstract: Bayesian model calibration is central to digital twins and computer experiments, as it aligns model outputs with field observations by estimating calibration parameters and correcting systematic model bias. Classical Bayesian calibration introduces latent parameters and a discrepancy function to model bias, but suffers from parameter--discrepancy confounding and is typically formulated as an offline procedure under a stationary data-generating assumption. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of Bayesian model calibration in digital twins and computer experiments, where systems change over time, by building an online calibration method that adapts to gradual and abrupt system changes, resulting in improved model accuracy. The researchers developed an online Bayesian calibration framework that can handle non-stationary data. This may be relevant to IT work in managing cloud infrastructure for digital twin applications.

case_studies.title: AI Engineering Blueprint for On-Premises Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
case_studies.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems are gaining traction in enterprise settings, yet stringent data protection regulations prevent many organizations from using cloud-based services, necessitating on-premises deployments. While existing blueprints and reference architectures focus on cloud deployments and lack enterprise-grade components, comprehensive on-premises implementation frameworks remain scarce. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of implementing retrieval-augmented generation systems on-premises, where the authors built a comprehensive AI engineering blueprint for scalable enterprise solutions, resulting in a framework for secure and compliant on-premises deployments. The blueprint addresses common challenges in on-premises RAG system implementation. It provides a structured approach to designing and deploying RAG systems within enterprise settings.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage on-premises infrastructure for organizations with strict data protection regulations, here is what to do: review the proposed AI engineering blueprint for potential application, assess your current RAG system deployment for scalability and security, and consider integrating the blueprint's enterprise-grade components to improve compliance.

case_studies.title: FedAttr: Towards Privacy-preserving Client-Level Attribution in Federated LLM Fine-tuning
case_studies.abstract: Watermark radioactivity testing type of methods can detect whether a model was trained on watermarked documents, and have become key tools for protecting data ownership in the fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs). Existing works have proved their effectiveness in centralized LLM fine-tuning. However, this type of method faces several challenges and remains underexplored in federated learning (FL), a widely-applied paradigm for fine-tuning LLMs collaboratively on private data across different users. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of protecting data ownership in federated learning for large language models, by building a method called FedAttr, and the result is a more privacy-preserving client-level attribution in federated LLM fine-tuning. The method aims to detect whether a model was trained on watermarked documents, even in a collaborative and private data setting. This research is relevant to IT work related to data privacy and security in cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: NeuroAgent: LLM Agents for Multimodal Neuroimaging Analysis and Research
case_studies.abstract: Multimodal neuroimaging analysis often involves complex, modality-specific preprocessing workflows that require careful configuration, quality control, and coordination across heterogeneous toolchains. Beyond preprocessing, downstream statistical analysis and disease classification commonly require task-specific code, evaluation protocols, and data-format conventions, creating additional barriers between raw acquisitions and reproducible scientific analysis. We present NeuroAgent, an LLM-driven agentic framework that automates key preprocessing and analysis steps for heterogeneous neuroimaging
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of complex and time-consuming neuroimaging analysis by building an automated framework called NeuroAgent. NeuroAgent automates key preprocessing and analysis steps for heterogeneous neuroimaging data. The result is a more efficient and reproducible scientific analysis process.
